name: Janet Freeman-Daily
summary: Janet Freeman-Daily learned she had lung cancer in 2011.
She first had chemotherapy and radiation. The cancer later spread outside her chest, and then to her other lung.
On 25 September 2012, the University of Colorado told her that her tumour had a ROS1 gene change.
She was eligible for a trial of a daily pill called crizotinib.
She started that trial in November 2012 in Denver.
A University of Colorado article dated 3 June 2025 quotes her account of meeting Paul Bunn, MD, there.
This page uses her own words for how she is now.

quotes.text: But on this date, the University of Colorado notified me that my tumor tissue tested positive for a gene rearrangement called ROS1, and I was eligible for a clinical trial of the targeted therapy pill crizotinib.
quotes.label: her blog post of 25 September 2025

quotes.text: Today I’m still on the same daily pill.
quotes.label: her blog post of 25 September 2025

quotes.text: I’ve been on the same oral therapy (with a couple of dose reductions) for over thirteen years. My scans have shown no sign of cancer since I started on that drug.

actions.what: Started the crizotinib trial in Denver
actions.quote: a series of amazing coincidences and good timing resulted in my cancer testing positive for the ROS1 biomarker and my getting one of the last slots in the associated clinical trial, which I started in November 2012 in Denver.

actions.what: Flew between Seattle and Denver for the trial
actions.quote: The first year or so after starting the trial, my energies were consumed with flying back and forth between Seattle and Denver for the trial, dealing with side effects, and coping with scanxiety every couple of months.

phase_links.cause: A new tumour appeared outside her chest, in lymph nodes on her collarbone. Her oncologist said they could “try again for a cure.”

sources.quote: However, a new tumor popped up outside my chest a few months after treatment ended. A PET scan detected “hot” lymph nodes on my collarbone, and a biopsy confirmed they contained lung cancer.
My oncologist said we could try again for a cure.
